version.author: Justin Johnson
version.changelog: ReEQ2 is here: a new interface, decramped filters up to 30 kHz and per-band dynamic EQ with sidechain inputs. Install "ReEQ2" from Extensions > ReaPack > Browse packages. It comes with an action to move your projects over with all their settings: search the Actions window for "ReEQ upgrade". This update changes nothing in ReEQ 1.2, so your projects sound exactly as before.

version.author: Justin Johnson
version.changelog: ReEQ2: a new interface, decramped filters to 30 kHz and per-band dynamic EQ - Redesigned interface: node panel with machined dials, Shape and Stereo pickers, node action card, Analyzer, Settings and Range popovers, gradient meters with clip alerts - Decramped Ivantsov filters replace the SVFs and Eco/HQ oversampling, matching the analogue curve up to Nyquist - Per-band dynamic EQ for bells and shelves: threshold, ratio, range, Auto or manual timing, sidechain inputs (channels 3/4, 5/6, 7/8), an unlinked detector with its own node, Listen, and optional lookahead - Analyser drawn per pixel with Fill, Line and Heat displays; curve-based auto gain; input trim - Embedded TCP/MCP view Includes an action that moves projects from ReEQ 1.2 over with all their settings: search the Actions window for "ReEQ upgrade". ReEQ 1.2 stays available as its own package.

version.author: Justin Johnson
version.changelog: Lower CPU: roughly 40-50% less with a typical handful of bands and 10-15% less with 14-16, with exactly the same sound - Bands that aren't moving skip their per-sample glide update - The output Mid/Side gain stage is skipped when it does nothing - Faster filter sections when many bands run in series

version.author: Justin Johnson
version.changelog: Set any value exactly with the new value stepper - Double-click a dial, dynamics knob or toolbar field to open it: each digit has up and down arrows (hold to repeat, or use the mouse wheel over a digit), with a sign column where the value can be negative - Changes apply as you click; values stay within each control's range; the revert icon puts back the value you started with - Cmd+double-click (Ctrl on Windows) resets any dial, knob or field to its default, the dynamics knobs included - Undo and automation now record the new value when you drag a panel dial
